_what: Gate B (docs/evidence-lane-plan.md §7). Deterministic Coverage@B, no LLM judge.

corpora.baseline: data/engine.prod-20260730.db — prod backup, 305 episodes / 1708 fragments, NO research episodes
corpora.with_evidence: data/engine.gateb.db — baseline + 30 research episodes (eval/gold_evidence.jsonl + eval/evidence_corpus.jsonl), refined + consolidated + swept. 7 kind='evidence' members, 6 attachments (3 entail / 2 contradict / 1 neutral). Built by scratchpad/gate_b_build.py; consolidation cost $0.00 on free-tier openrouter.

verdict: PASS on the stated criterion — self-lane coverage does not regress anywhere when evidence enters the corpus or when the lane is switched on.
_caveats: The +6.2 narrow (75.0 -> 81.2, tail 67 -> 83) is NOT evidence that the partition works.
Coverage@B scores whether the assembled context covers the gold's key_facts; it cannot
tell a fact covered by the user's own note from one covered by a source. The topical
sources in evidence_corpus.jsonl were written around the gold's subject matter, so they
legitimately cover some key_facts. Read the gain as 'added content covered more facts',
LANE=0 and LANE=1 are identical on all three sets, which means the partition was not
meaningfully exercised rather than proven inert: only 6 of 44 gold queries surfaced an
Evidence section at all, and none of those carried a computed verdict (the co-surfaced
claim was never also in the result set). At 30 research episodes against 1097 self
fragments, evidence simply does not reach the budget often enough to crowd anything out.
Re-run this once real evidence volume is closer to note volume — that is when
EVIDENCE_SHARE starts to bind and this comparison becomes informative.
